candidate: Tune draft depth; do not maximize it
cautions: ByteShape draft3-to5 improved decode; Flash MTP2-to4 regressed. ByteShape draft9 failed the64K reserve. Its32K fallback is not a controlled draft5-to9 comparison or a universal diminishing-returns curve.
takeaway: Increasing speculative draft depth can improve or reduce decode speed. Test a bounded range and retain the fastest setting that meets memory and quality constraints; larger drafts are not automatically better.

candidate: Check memory on every device under load
cautions: Observed reserve failures are not necessarily CUDA OOMs. The recorded768MiB guard is a campaign rule, not a universal reserve; short-probe fit does not certify full-context quality or sustained concurrent operation.
takeaway: Model weights fitting is only the first memory check. Verify each GPU under the intended context, batch, draft depth and concurrency, retaining working headroom. Record failed fits and context reductions as separate configurations.

candidate: Tune threads to the actual CPU allocation
cautions: Ollama128-to12 threads helped in one12-CPU L40 allocation; V100 decode2-to4 changed less than0.5%. Neither establishes a universal thread count. [Scheduler-level causes were not isolated.]
takeaway: Inspect the CPUs allocated to the process and the threads the runtime actually uses. More threads can be neutral or harmful even for GPU inference; test an allocation-aware setting rather than maximizing thread count.

candidate: Tune batches against speed and memory together
cautions: Flash V100 microbatch evidence supports this tradeoff, not a universally optimal batch size. Automatic fit could also change placement, so the measured configuration tradeoff does not isolate a single kernel mechanism.
takeaway: Larger prefill batches or microbatches can trade better prompt processing for slower decode and less free GPU memory. Measure both phases and peak memory at the intended workload before retaining a larger batch.

cautions: At fixed MTP3, temperature1-to0.5 improved short decode2.51% and changed long decode-0.37%. Combined temperature/draft changes do not isolate temperature. Temperature0 seeds are timing repeats, not independent stochastic samples.
takeaway: Temperature changes model sampling as well as the experiment. Do not silently lower it to gain speed; measure its effect separately from draft depth and validate completed answers. Lower temperature is not a reliable universal speed setting.

candidate: Measure speculation throughput, not acceptance alone
cautions: Both the controlled V100 MTP3-to5 pair and L40 Glimmer combination ran faster with lower accepted/proposed fractions. Glimmer also changed temperature. [Draft and verification costs were not separately timed.]
takeaway: Use draft-acceptance counters to diagnose speculation, but rank candidates by measured decode time and memory fit. Acceptance fraction alone can rank candidates incorrectly because it does not measure the cost or benefit of the whole speculative step.

candidate: Keep decode speed and request latency distinct
cautions: Glimmer long probes gained4.82% decode but took3.78% more request time. These are two capped repeats, not completed tasks. Flash and cross-engine comparisons change multiple settings; loading and queue time are excluded.
takeaway: Choose the optimization objective explicitly and measure both inference phases. Higher decode throughput can coexist with slower prefill and longer total requests; report that tradeoff even when decode is the primary objective.

candidate: Retain repeats and test representative lengths
cautions: Glimmer long candidate repeats ranged110.62-148.64t/s around a pooled126.84t/s. Only two repeats per length were available. [Repeatability and the cause of variation remain unresolved.]
takeaway: Keep repeat-level timings and evaluate short and long inputs separately. Small pooled gains amid large run-to-run variation are provisional; do not select a preset from its fastest sample or assume one prompt length predicts another.

candidate: Separate prefix reuse from raw prefill
cautions: Cache benefits require a reusable prefix and depend on runtime state. A stored-token counter is not automatically a reused-token counter; verify each API field. Do not divide the full prompt length by the time spent processing only its new suffix.
takeaway: Prefix caching can avoid most repeated prompt work without improving uncached prefill throughput. Record reused and newly processed tokens separately, and benchmark cold and reused-prefix requests as distinct workloads.

candidate: Separate concurrency, throughput and user latency
cautions: Glimmer shared/separate comparisons changed topology and runtime, and historical task times were single observations. [The optimal concurrency or replica layout for another workload is unestablished.]
takeaway: More concurrent requests or replicas do not guarantee faster individual requests. Measure completed workload wall time and each request latency under the actual GPU topology; overlapping per-request token rates must not be summed into server throughput.

candidate: Check completed work after a token-rate win
cautions: ByteShape MTP5 generated more tokens and finished one short check later despite faster decode. Glimmer native and fixed-probe rankings differed. These bounded checks do not establish broad model quality or production-workflow speedups.
takeaway: Fixed-output probes measure token generation, while naturally completed tasks measure useful work. Check correctness, generated length and completion time separately: faster decode may produce a longer answer or rank configurations differently from a real workflow.

candidate: Separate default repair from feature gains
cautions: L40 thread correction and matched llama.cpp MTP toggle each contributed substantially. The full Ollama-to-llama.cpp comparison also changes context, KV, batching, templates and placement; it does not isolate an agent or speculation effect.
takeaway: Keep untouched defaults, resource-aware corrections and within-runtime feature controls distinct. A full optimized preset can be much faster, but only matched comparisons support attributing the gain to a particular change.

candidate: Revalidate settings on the destination runtime and hardware
cautions: V100/L40 differ in CPU platforms, power, defaults and sometimes workloads. Kernel comparisons also changed runtime packages, so MMQ effects are not isolated. Exploratory records are not deployable profiles. [A portable optimum is unestablished.]
takeaway: Transfer candidate settings as hypotheses, then verify the destination GPU, CPU allocation, runtime build and libraries, model placement and workload. Effective defaults and kernel behavior can change across systems; identical model bytes do not make speedups portable.

candidate: Verify effective settings before counting experiments
cautions: This pinned Glimmer DFlash path caps drafts at15 for its16-position block. Requested17 was replaced before timing. The cap is implementation-specific and does not establish a universal speculative limit or performance optimum.
takeaway: Read the runtime-resolved settings and supported model limits. A requested flag can be clamped or rejected; record the value actually executed and never count an unexecuted or duplicate effective setting as a distinct benchmark.

candidate: Validate model output channels and answer correctness separately
cautions: All three Glimmer short final answers matched after correct channel extraction; raw bodies remained non-JSON and original parser failures were retained. One short check per configuration is not broad or full-context quality evidence.
takeaway: Parse the model-specific final-answer channel before checking task correctness, while retaining raw responses and endpoint-format checks. Reasoning text, an HTTP success or a capped output does not establish a valid completed answer.

candidate: Preserve the meaning of every throughput number
cautions: Recorded Ollama decode uses n/time; llama.cpp uses(n-1)/time. Templates also change token counts. CANON representative pairs remain individual observations. Unknown cache state cannot be promoted to confirmed cold-prefill evidence.
takeaway: Record formatted input/output token counts, phase durations, cache state and the engine timing convention. Pool compatible runs using summed timed tokens divided by summed phase time, and keep individual observations distinct from pooled results.
